findings.message: Scope-in requires `compose_pipeline` (squatch/merge.py:450) to receive the one shared registry/cooldown payload and live Timers instead of constructing an independent registry. Under the no-dual-path rule that makes the payload a required argument. Several existing direct callers are outside the fence and would break the `uv run pytest -q` Verification command: tests/test_merge.py (lines 92, 739), tests/test_mergequeue.py (lines 717, 780, 939, 1000), tests/test_daemon_composition.py (line 342), eval/shakeout/bench.py (line 82) and eval/daemon_soak.py (line 387).
findings.paved_road: Add every direct `compose_pipeline` caller to the fence and the ownership hooks: tests/test_merge.py, tests/test_mergequeue.py, tests/test_daemon_composition.py, eval/shakeout/bench.py and eval/daemon_soak.py. Each supplies one payload and Timers built over its existing journal and clock, following the admission-holds-activation precedent for the mandatory inbox. List the large ones as measured on-demand inspection exceptions. Add a criterion that the listed callers pass the shared payload and keep their existing assertions.

findings.message: The existing `test_main_restart_delegates_real_reconcile_once_before_first_offer` asserts `len(owned) == 1` Timers for both the `run` and `drain` verbs, with the restart-composed Timers already created inside the drain session. The scope-in line 'Bootstrap drain creates and shuts it down at its root' reads as a second, root-level Timers construction. That would contradict the preserved assertion and double-fire expired deadlines on rearm.
findings.paved_road: State that the bootstrap drain's payload binds the single Timers instance created by `restart_session` / `compose_daemon_timers` for that lock-held session (no second construction). Keep the criterion that `test_restart_timers.py` preserves exactly one owned Timers per session.
